description: deixis N[T] parts vectors — complete compose/decompose (ADR 0009 §6, R0/R1) and contexts, replacement and complete cuts (§7). Hand-authored from docs/design/0009-optional-node-values.md alone, per vectors/NODE-PLAN.md; not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Spelling as in NODE-PLAN.md, plus: a decompose result is {parts:{own, children}}, a different type from a node although its fields match; a hole is {hole:{}} standing in for the WHOLE subtree at its position (own value included); a context or skeleton is a node spelling with holes; a cut's subtree map is a list of [path, node] pairs, a path being a list of hex keys. Results are compared structurally: holes must be at the same positions, and nodes and values use the equality of node-identity.json. Under ADR 0010 this file reads as the explicit optional instantiation Node[Option[fixture]], with the tag-respecting option slot of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; every case here holds there under the mandatory core's generic laws (checked case by case on 2026-09-23; see NODE-PLAN.md).

cases.name: decompose-valued-node-returns-own-and-complete-children
cases.note: X7/C3. §6: decompose_N(Node(o,m)) = (o,m). The map contains every immediate child with its exact key, including the unvalued one, and the parent's own value is returned separately, not dropped.

cases.name: decompose-childless-returns-empty-map
cases.note: X7. §6: a childless node returns an empty map, not a missing one.

cases.name: decompose-unvalued-empty-node
cases.note: X2/X7. Both parts are empty and are still present: (None, {}).

cases.name: decompose-children-are-whole-subtrees
cases.note: X7/C3. §6: the finite map contains whole immediate child subtrees, not just their own payloads. Returning only Some(a) for 6b would lose the grandchild.

cases.name: decompose-keeps-exact-keys
cases.note: C3/C4. The empty key, a non-UTF-8 key and an upper-case ASCII key all come back exactly. A decompose that decodes, folds or drops keys fails.

cases.name: compose-empty-parts
cases.note: X7. compose_N((None, {})) is the single unvalued node e (§9.2).

cases.name: split-retains-ancestor-value-and-siblings
cases.note: X9. §7: the context retains every ancestor's optional own value (r), the keys leading to the hole, and every sibling subtree (6a). The subtree at the hole carries its own value (a) and its descendants.

cases.name: split-at-empty-path
cases.note: §7: at ε, the context is just the hole, and the subtree is the whole tree.

cases.name: split-deep-retains-both-ancestor-values
cases.note: X9/X10. A hole two levels down keeps BOTH ancestors' values (r and a). The subtree is the empty node, which is a real part.

cases.name: split-at-missing-path-is-undefined
cases.note: §7: plug_p(split_p(n)) ≡ n holds when p ∈ D_n. split_p is partial, and [6b] ∉ D_n.

cases.name: plug-replaces-and-keeps-context
cases.note: §7 replacement n[p := s]: plug the split context with a different subtree. at(n[p := s], p) ≡ s, and the ancestor value r and the sibling 6a are untouched. Replacing with the empty node removes the old subtree's value a and child 78, as replacement should.

cases.name: plug-into-root-hole
cases.note: §7: plugging s into the context at ε gives s.

cases.name: cut-at-two-siblings
cases.note: X8. §7: cut_F(n) = (skeleton_F(n), {p ↦ at(n,p) | p ∈ F}). The skeleton keeps the root value r above the holes; every distinction occurs in the skeleton or a supplied subtree.

cases.name: cut-at-a-deeper-set-of-the-same-tree
cases.note: X8/X9. A different complete cut of the same tree. The own value a above a hole now lives in the skeleton (§7: this includes own values above holes). Paired with rebuild-from-deeper-cut.

cases.name: cut-with-a-missing-path-is-undefined
cases.note: §7 defines cut_F for F ⊆ D_n. [6b] ∉ D_n, so cut_F is undefined here; cut_F : N[T] ⇀ … is partial for exactly this reason. Silently skipping the missing path would be a fallback (§5).

cases.name: rebuild-from-sibling-cut
cases.note: X8. §7: rebuild_F(cut_F(n)) ≡ n, rebuilding from the cut-at-two-siblings output.

cases.name: rebuild-from-deeper-cut
cases.note: X8. §7: different complete cuts of the same tree reconstruct the same tree. The expected value is identical to rebuild-from-sibling-cut.
